author: John Donne
title: The Poems of John Donne, Volume I: The Text of the Poems with Appendixes
edition: Edited by Herbert J. C. Grierson. Oxford: Clarendon Press, 1912; Project Gutenberg 48688. Main poem text only; variant readings, notes, page/line numbers and stanza numerals omitted. HTML emphasis flattened; decorative drop capitals joined to their word; horizontal indentation normalized while original stanza and verse-line boundaries and old spelling are retained. The library text runs from The Printer to the Understanders and the other seventeenth-century prefatory matter through Appendixes A, B and C, including the Elegies upon the Author and Grierson's printed attributions of doubtful poems; Grierson's Preface, Note, contents, frontispiece and caption, the side-notes and footnotes, and the Index of First Lines are omitted. Stanza numerals printed inside a stanza (as in A Hymne to God the Father) are omitted; numbered poems keep their numerals as headings. The transcriber reports modernising long s, correcting 'foveraigne' to 'soveraigne' on page 262, and writing out abbreviated -que endings in the Latin text on pages 390-392.

rights.basis: The English text in this 1912 edition was published before 1931; its US publication copyright term has expired as of 2026. The linked primary transcription/catalogue identifies its US public-domain status. No later editorial introduction is included.

acquisition.method: Project Gutenberg HTML (pglaf mirror of ebook 48688, pg48688-images.html). Kept the text between the Gutenberg separators from THE PRINTER heading up to INDEX OF FIRST LINES. Removed page numbers, line numbers, Note links, variant-reading (ind1) and footnote divisions, side-notes, the frontispiece figure and footnote-call superscripts; joined each decorative drop capital to its word (a space kept only where the capital is itself a word, as in I WONDER); flattened emphasis and dropped the indentation classes. Each stanza division became a stanza block, one verse line per line; section and poem titles became headings; prose paragraphs and title lines became paragraphs with whitespace collapsed.
